original_test_intent: Write one approved unique MAC address to the correct management-interface EEPROM, verify persistent identity and reachability, and prove the other interface and unrelated inventory were unchanged.
original_method: Master provides OEM 0x30/0x40 and selector mapping but omits MAC bytes. Review preserves it and requires the firmware-matched full payload, persistent readback and independent recovery.
manual_activity: Owner validates interface/EEPROM mapping, allocates a unique policy-compliant MAC, approves the exact bytes and provides independent OOB/console access plus original-value restore.
required_inputs: Interface selector and EEPROM region mapping
Approved unique target MAC and byte order
safety_requirements: Do not use sshpass or disabled host verification
Capture both interfaces and EEPROM baseline
Verify EEPROM and runtime identity separately
Do not power-cycle or retry automatically
Stop on lost access or mismatch
agent_execution_scope: Present network blast radius for confirmation
Read persistent EEPROM and runtime LAN state
engineer_actions: Approve target MAC, payload, downtime and recovery
Authorize restoration and own final DUT verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unsafe and incomplete: selector-only 0x30/0x40 cannot encode the named MAC write, insecure SSH exposes credentials, and lan print does not prove EEPROM persistence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Only after approval, use protected `ipmitool raw 0x30 0x40 <validated-selector> <vendor-defined-MAC-bytes>` exactly as documented, then independently read EEPROM and runtime LAN identity.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The original command family, selector values and 10/5 timing remain unchanged; no MAC or payload order is fabricated.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Back up persistent identity, validate a unique MAC and complete payload, perform one confirmed EEPROM write, then prove persistent/runtime value, reachability and non-target isolation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the omitted MAC bytes, allocation control, persistent readback and recovery without changing Master.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: lan print alone cannot establish EEPROM programming or persistence, and read-only inspection cannot satisfy the write objective.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong interface, byte order or duplicate MAC can sever management access or create a network conflict; recovery must not depend on the changed interface.

project_override_considerations: A vendor utility is equivalent only if it writes the same EEPROM field with allocation, persistence and reachability evidence and records whether raw 0x30/0x40 remains untested.
expected_evidence: Approved unique MAC and complete payload
Pre-write persistent/runtime identity and recovery proof

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title requires a MAC write, but Master and DeepSeek send only a selector and accept generic LAN output. The required MAC payload, persistence proof and recovery are absent; DeepSeek also uses insecure access.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The persistent identity objective and selector concept are clear. Complete vendor schema, allocated value, recovery and approval are execution-readiness inputs rather than an irreducible review blocker.

review_improvement: Defines the missing payload, persistent target, uniqueness policy, independent recovery and non-target audit while preventing read-only evidence from being credited as write coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Changing a management MAC couples nonvolatile storage, runtime network identity and external address allocation. Correctness therefore requires proof at all three layers. A selector-only request cannot express the approved identity, and a runtime LAN display can remain stale or reflect a different storage source, so it cannot be the sole oracle.
